chapter_theme: The making of the embryo (கரு உற்பத்தி): the Lord, knowing each soul's due, builds its body in the womb from the tattvas and the breaths through the union of the parents; the state of breath and seed at conception decides sex, lifespan and defects; the parents do not know what they make, and the Lord, present though unseen in the small body, shapes and protects it by grace.
structure_note: The chapter moves from the Lord forming the body from the tattvas (451 to 460), through images of its building (house 461, machines 467, kiln 468, bubble and light 472) and the senses and faculties (473, 474), to grace and the parents' love (475 to 477), the effects of breath and the mother's state at conception (478 to 484), and closing reflections on maya and the Lord within (485 to 491).

451.reading: The Lord, the First, our precious life, makes the twenty-five that were set apart before; staying within the globe of the womb he forms the embryo, knowing what it is to become.
451.nuance: இருபத்தஞ்சு (twenty-five) is traditionally taken as the tattvas from earth up to purusha that make up the soul's body. ஆவது அறிந்தே, knowing what it will become, is usually read as his knowing the soul's karma before shaping the body.

452.reading: Above the root he sets fire and water, joins the red foot of knowledge, and, so that the sweet life borne there may enter, he lays on it the burden of the ten.
452.nuance: மூலம் (the root) is taken as the muladhara, அங்கி and அப்பு as fire and water, and பத்து as the ten vital airs, though ten months is also possible. செந்தாள் (red foot) and பறிகின்ற are obscure.

453.reading: At the hour when the two join in pleasure, the Lord, present in the sorrowful house of bondage that went before them, fixes in that moment of love the span of time and the life on earth the child will have.
453.nuance: The verse puts the fixing of the lifespan (காலமும்) and the earthly life (வாழ்க்கையும்) at the moment of conception. Whose bondage the துயர்மனை is, the parents' or the soul's, is not clear.

454.reading: Those freed from birth have seen that the 'four and three sevens' join in the man's body, which others do not know; the form that sought and entered the womb fell as two.
454.nuance: நால் மூவேழ் is read either as 4 + 21 = 25, the tattvas of 451, or as some other count; I can't fix it. உருவம் இரண்டாக may mean the seed dividing, or twins, or the two parents' contributions.

455.reading: The seed falls and the womb opens; the first five, joined by the ten, rise, and the poured water, the elements and the faculties hide within at the brow and the crown.
455.nuance: லிங்கம் and யோனி are used plainly of the sexual organs here. The first five are taken as the elements and the ten as the senses or vital airs; நுதல் உச்சி (brow, crown) points to yogic centres where the faculties are said to lie latent.

456.reading: As the wind that has taken a flower's scent spreads it and holds it in the world, so the long subtle breath settled in the soul, at the marked moment, calls it and lets it go.
456.nuance: The plain image is clear: breath carries the soul as wind carries scent. What குறிக்கொண்ட போது (the marked time) and அவிழும் (opens, lets go) refer to, conception or the soul's leaving a former body, is not fixed by the verse.

457.reading: The eight that go out, the eighteen that come in, the freed one sunk within, the nine gates, the serpent with the eight and the four horses: if the driver does not let go, it becomes even a pig.
457.nuance: A list of the body's parts as a chariot team. The numbers are traditionally matched with breaths, tattvas and senses, and the last line with birth in a low body, but I can't fix any of them. The same verse stands as 2926 with a different second line.

458.reading: If the forces meet rising, the child will be like the Lord; if they meet reversed, like Hari; if they are kept level, of balanced understanding; and a son matching his name will rule a great kingdom.
458.nuance: The subject of ஏற, மாற, நேரொக்க is unstated; it is usually taken as the breath or the seed at conception. The variant அரியயன் would make the second Brahma, or Hari and Brahma together.

459.reading: From the mingled essence of the two, the flowing seed takes form; once the body, compounded of many things, is settled, the mind sinks into a stupor mixed with maya.
459.nuance: ஏயம் and சாயம் are unclear; சாயம் may be colour or essence. மனோலயம் mixed with maya is usually read as the soul losing awareness in the womb.

460.reading: In the womb maya joins her brood to the soul in its kevala state; turiya is broken and thought arises; karma takes firm hold and maya's bonds begin, as the word of the pure Veda says.
460.nuance: கேவலம் (the soul's isolated state, bound only by anava), துரியம், காமியம் (karma) and மாயேயம் (the products of maya) are Siddhanta terms; the verse seems to describe the soul passing from kevala to its embodied (sakala) state at conception. எட்டாதல் is obscure.

461.reading: He wove bones together, bound them with nerves like lashings, made a fitting house of red flesh, and set in it, sweetly, the seat of life; I seek that good one, the Lord who rises there.
461.nuance: The body is described as a house built by the Lord, bone for frame, nerve for cord, flesh for walls, and the poet seeks the builder who dwells in it. The variant நண்பால் would make the last line 'I seek him in friendship'.

462.reading: The milk-coloured one, bright as the sun, who brings things to ripeness, enters the whole body for its good, calms the rage of the fire below, ordains how it should be, and leaves.
462.nuance: பால்வண்ணன் is an epithet of Siva. The 'fire' of குதம் is read as the heat of the lower body or womb, which would harm the embryo if not checked. The verse's subject may be the Lord or the sun as his agent.

463.reading: When the deeds that bring many endings came due, the Lord took the embryo of bondage, which does much that is blamed, through its many turns and kept it from being burned.
463.nuance: Line 2 (வழிபல நீராடி வைத்தெழு வாங்கி) is obscure. The point taken is that the embryo, formed by karma, is protected in the heat of the womb by the Lord.

464.reading: The white seed in its channel and the womb in its order: entering eight finger-breadths and coming out four, and with the eight letters, it becomes a body of eight spans.
464.nuance: The body measuring eight of its own spans is an old teaching. எண்விரல், நால்விரல் (eight and four finger-breadths) are often read of the breath's reach, and அக்கரம் எட்டும் is obscure.

465.reading: The pure one who entered there in the act of love, whose work of giving set a body in the sheath, there in that one act made an egg of two eights and three fives.
465.nuance: இரண்டெட்டு மூன்றைந்து (sixteen and fifteen) is commonly matched with the kalas of the moon and sun, or other counts; I can't fix it. முட்டை (egg) names the embryo. The variant கோகத்துள் would replace கோசத்துள் (in the sheath).

466.reading: The five foolish senses within the body arise and die within the body; in the same way the soul within the cosmos is born and dies there, and the Lord rests in the cosmos's nada.
466.nuance: பிண்டம் (body) and அண்டம் (cosmos) are set side by side as microcosm and macrocosm. Who அமர்ந்திருந்தான் refers to, the Lord or the soul, is not stated.

467.reading: The Lord built my body like machines: raising the leaf-machine, planting the embryo with the five in the balance-machine, fixing the thirty in the standing machine, and making one thing of the nine in the forge-machine.
467.nuance: பொறி (machine, contrivance) repeats in every line. The numbers five, thirty and nine are matched by tradition with elements, tattvas and openings, but the verse does not say what they are.

468.reading: From the clay the two set in their pleasure, one alone forms the pot of sorrow; with nine water-jars and eighteen pots, the kiln fires and it is made.
468.nuance: A potter's image: the parents supply clay, the Lord is the potter, the womb the kiln. ஒன்பது and பதினெட்டு may be the nine openings and some count of parts.

469.reading: You don't know how the body came to be, you don't set apart the qualities that grow in it, you don't go into them; the body is what took shape within the ten, so that what was set within it might be known.
469.nuance: ஈரைந்து (ten) is usually the ten months in the womb. சித்திகள் இட்டது may be powers placed in the body or simply what was set there; the last line is compressed.

470.reading: The way he set the body and the way he set the life, placing the nine gates as sluices, and the Lord who set the fire at the end within the firm lotus at the head: I have joined hands with him.
470.nuance: The nine gates are the body's openings, here called மடை, sluices built to purpose. The lotus at the head with fire is a yogic image of the crown. The verse treats the body's design as the Lord's work and the place where the poet meets him.

471.reading: I have heard it: the great unfailing light everywhere is the one who kindles it; the first maker of wombs, the divine builder, joins the fluid into the embryo's form and draws it out until it comes right in the body.
471.nuance: மயன் is the divine architect of the Puranas, here used of the Lord as maker of wombs (முதல் யோனி). The construction of line 1 is loose.

472.reading: Once flower and bud have joined and opened, a light within the grove mingles and is born; like a bubble standing in water, a shadow, it spreads through the earthly body, and the eight take hold.
472.nuance: காவுடைத் தீபம் (the lamp of the grove) is obscure. The eight are taken in the next verse as five senses and three inner faculties, the subtle body (puriyattaka) of the tradition.

473.reading: Of the eight, five become the senses and three the bound inner faculties; this body-bag, which is the bond's awareness clinging to the soul, the Lord with the eye in his brow ties, unties and watches.
473.nuance: கரணம் மூன்று are traditionally mind, intellect and ego. Calling the body பாச உணர்வு, the awareness of the bond, makes it the means by which the soul knows while bound.

474.reading: Joining his name with it, the Lord with the brow eye fashions the body, and so that the soul's bond may fall away he lays out the whole range the Veda describes, starting from earth.
474.nuance: The body is made so that பசுபாசம் நீங்கிட, the bond may leave the soul: embodiment is for release. மண்முதலாக is read as the tattvas from earth upward. கண்ணுதல் நாமம் கலந்து is unclear.

475.reading: There is nothing but grace, and no grace apart from Hara; so when he gives a soul he also arranges the love that comes to it from its two mothers.
475.nuance: இருகைத் தாயர் is taken as the mother who bears and the one who nurses, or the mother and the divine mother; I can't fix it. The point is that a child's being loved is itself the Lord's grace.

476.reading: The birth so arranged is the greatness of the good Lady and of the Light who gathered and removed the darkness: they set out all the many beings given discernment and stand within them too.
476.nuance: மாது நல்லாள் is Shakti and சோதியவன் Siva. பகுத்துணர்வாக்கிய (made to discern) may refer to giving beings the faculties to know.

477.reading: The fire that grows into greatness, the fashioning seen as male, female or neither, and the likeness borne down the mother's and father's line: all these were brought about by the Light's power.
477.nuance: வன்னி (fire) is unclear: the vital heat of the embryo, or the Lord as fire. The variant வன்னியைக் makes it an object. கற்பனை here seems to mean form or fashioning, not fancy.

478.reading: If the male part prevails it becomes a male, if the female part a female, and if the two are equal neither; if the strength is great the child will rule the whole earth, and if the force is excessive nothing takes at all.
478.nuance: The first two lines state an old belief about sex determination. தாண் and பாணவம் are obscure; தாண் may be a misreading of தாள் (strength).

479.reading: If after the flow the breath runs five, life will be a hundred years; if four, eighty on earth; the yogi who discerns the flowing breath this way can also direct its flow.
479.nuance: Five and four are usually taken as the reach of the breath in finger-breadths at the moment of union. The last line turns the teaching toward breath control.

480.reading: If the flowing breath falls short the child is a dwarf, if it is twisted lame, if it is caught midway hunchbacked; and this, looked at closely, does not lie with the woman's breath.
480.nuance: விளைக்கின் is read as 'bends' or 'twists'. The last line is unclear: it may say that the woman's breath does not decide these things, or that women have none of this.

481.reading: If the mother's belly is heavy with faeces the child is dull, if with urine mute, and if both are equal blind: this for the child that has come into the mother's belly.
481.nuance: மலம் and சலம் here are faeces and urine, not the Siddhanta impurity. The verse states a physiological belief about the mother's condition at conception or in pregnancy.

482.reading: The child is male if the breath is on the right, female if on the left, two if the downward breath opposes, and neither if the breaths taken are equal.
482.nuance: The verse does not name its subject; tradition takes வலம், இடம் as the right and left nostril or channel. அபானன் is the downward breath of yoga physiology.

483.reading: If the good breath rises evenly in both, the child conceived will be fair; if it falters in both, the bangled woman conceives nothing.
483.nuance: The variant ஒத்தேறில் (rises together) fits the sense.

484.reading: The child conceived in the bangled woman's belly is a light trembling within; nourished as with milk, it grows within like the sun's golden form and takes its fitting shape.
484.nuance: தால்வளை (perhaps the curve of the womb) and பால் வளர்ந்து are obscure. The light image echoes 471.

485.reading: The form grows for ten bright months and comes into the world in its season; it grows mingled with maya, and who here knows how it comes to be without form?
485.nuance: அருவமதாவது may mean how the embodied one becomes formless again at death, or how the formless Lord is in it; both readings stand.

486.reading: He who planted the seed did not know, she who received it did not see, the smith who knew told no one, and the Supreme who tells things as they are is there too: I am lost; how low is this maya!
486.nuance: தட்டான், the goldsmith who shapes, is taken as Brahma the fashioner or as the Lord himself; பரமன் then is the Supreme behind him. The point is that the parents have no knowledge of what they make.

487.reading: Born of two who met seeking pleasure and grown within painful bondage, once born into the world one can still seek the Ancient and stand there chanting.
487.nuance: Lines 3 and 4 play on நாடி (seeking) and are loose; the variant சிந்தித்து (thinking) for சந்தித்து changes the first line slightly. The reading that birth from bondage still permits worship is mine.

488.reading: If a cuckoo's egg is put in a crow's nest, the crow raises it without suspicion; it does not go, does not leave, does not ask why: the crow raises it out of delusion.
488.nuance: The verse states only the image. Placed here it is taken as parents raising a child whose soul is not theirs, in the delusion that it is.

489.reading: As the root-tuber becomes a sprout, shoots up, becomes a bush and then fruit and gives, and in each stage is the sweetness proper to it, so the First Lord stands as each thing to each thing.
489.nuance: அதற்கது வாய் (being that to that) is the key phrase: the Lord is present in every stage of growth as what that stage is. The image continues the chapter's growth of the embryo.

490.reading: Though our Lord's greatness is beyond all others, he is mingled within the smallness of flesh; Mahadeva is beyond the measure of the gods' knowing, and is known within tapas.
490.nuance: தானே அறியும் may mean that he alone knows himself, or that he is known of himself within tapas. ஊனே சிறுமையுள் sets the great Lord in the small body.

491.reading: The subtle body that had dissolved into the Supreme takes form again so this body may grow, and by grace is shaped anew and born, as salt crystallizes out of the sea.
491.nuance: The salt image is of something dissolved that takes form again from the same water. பரத்திற் கரைந்து பதிந்த நற்காயம் is read as the subtle body resting in the Supreme between births.

links.note: The same verse appears twice: 2926 reads ஆகிப் படைத்தன in line 2 where 457 reads மூழ்கின்ற முத்தனும், and 457's recorded variants are 2926's readings.
Both list the body as bone, sinew and flesh. The Naladiyar asks which of these parts is the woman a man desires; Tirumular sees in the same parts a house built by the Lord and seeks its builder.

Both describe the body by its nine openings. The Naladiyar makes it a pot seeping filth and calls the man who admires it a fool; Tirumular makes the nine gates sluices set by the Lord, who dwells at its crown and is met there. The conflict is over the body's worth and depends on reading 470 as valuing the body, not only describing how it was made.
725 says Tirumular once thought the body a blemish, then found the Lord had made it his temple, and so cherishes it; 470 already finds the Lord set within the body he built.
Both use the seed or tuber and its sprout: 1932 says seed and sprout exist only together, 489 that the Lord is present as each stage of the growth.

source_issues: 457 repeats 2926 except for line 2; its variants (ஆகிப்படைத்தன, விடாவிடிற், பந்தியு) are 2926's readings, and பன்றி (pig) against பந்தி (row) changes the sense of the last line.
478: தாண் and பாணவம் are obscure and may be corrupt; தாண் may stand for தாள்.
452 line 2 (செந்தாள்), 463 line 2, 464 line 4 (அக்கரம் எட்டும்) and 472 line 2 (காவுடைத் தீபம்) are obscure.
